Main.sentence: Deepwater drilling ,  or deep well drilling ,  is the process of creating holes in the ___E:Earth's crust U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth%27s_crust)___ using a ___E:drilling rig U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drilling_rig)___ for ___E:oil extraction U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_extraction)___ under the deep sea. There are approximately 3400 deepwater wells in the ___E:Gulf of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico)___ with depths greater than 150 meters.  [full citation needed]
Deepwater drilling has not been technologically or economically feasible for many years, but with rising oil prices, [when?] more companies are investing in this sector.

Major investors include ___E:Halliburton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halliburton)___ , ___E:Diamond Offshore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond_Offshore_Drilling)___ , ___E:Transocean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transocean)___ , ___E:Geoservices U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoservices)___ , and ___E:Schlumberger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlumberger)___ .

The deepwater gas and oil market has been back on the rise since the 2010 Deepwater Horizon disaster, with total expenditures of around ___E:US$ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar)___ 35 billion per year in the market and total global ___E:capital expenditures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_expenditure)___ of US$167 billion in the past four years.

Industry analysis by business intelligence company ___E:Visiongain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Visiongain&action=edit&redlink=1)___ estimated in 2011 that total expenditures in global deepwater infrastructure would reach US$145 billion.
A ___E:HowStuffWorks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HowStuffWorks)___ article explains how and why deepwater drilling is practiced:
Not all oil is accessible on land or in shallow water.
You can find some oil deposits buried deep under the ___E:ocean floor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seabed)___ . ...

Using sonic equipment, oil companies determine the drilling sites most likely to produce oil. Then they use a mobile ___E:offshore drilling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offshore_drilling)___ unit (MODU) to dig the initial well. Some units are converted into production rigs, meaning they switch from drilling for oil to capturing oil once it's found.
Most of the time, the oil company will replace the MODU with a more permanent oil production rig to capture oil. ...The MODU's job is to drill down into the ocean's floor to find oil deposits.
The part of the drill that extends below the deck and through the water is called the ___E:riser U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drilling_riser)___ .

The riser allows for ___E:drilling fluids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drilling_fluid)___ to move between the floor and the rig. Engineers lower a ___E:drill string U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drill_string)___ – a series of pipes designed to drill down to the oil deposit – through the riser.

In the ___E:Deepwater Horizon oil spill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepwater_Horizon_oil_spill)___ of 2010, a large explosion occurred, killing workers and ___E:spilling oil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_spill)___ into the Gulf of Mexico while a BP oil rig was drilling in ___E:deep waters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelagic_zone)___ .
The expansion of deepwater drilling is happening despite accidents in offshore fields ...
Despite the risks, the deepwater drilling trend is spreading in the Mediterranean and off the coast of East Africa after a string of huge discoveries of natural gas. ...
The reason for the resumption of such drilling, analysts say, is continuing high demand for energy worldwide.

Drilling in deep waters can be performed by two main types of mobile deepwater drilling rigs: ___E:semi-submersible U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-submersible)___ drilling rigs and ___E:drillships U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drillship)___ .

Drilling can also be performed from a fixed-position installation such as a fixed platform, or a floating platform, such as a ___E:spar platform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spar_(platform))___ , a ___E:tension-leg platform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tension-leg_platform)___ , or a semi-submersible production platform.

On 20 April 2010, a ___E:BP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BP)___ deepwater oil rig ( ___E:Deepwater Horizon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepwater_Horizon)___ ) exploded, killing 11 and releasing 750,000 cubic meters (200 million gallons) of oil into the Gulf of Mexico.
With those numbers, many scientists consider this disaster to be one of the worst environmental disasters in the history of the US.

A large number of animal deaths have resulted from the release of the oil. A Center study estimates that over 82,000 birds, about 6,000 sea turtles, and nearly 26,000 marine mammals were killed from either the initial explosion or the oil spill. ___E:Deepwater wellbore integrity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepwater_wellbore_integrity)___ has become an increasingly important point in the field of petroleum engineering.
